mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) above 4.5% for two consecutive months signals a restrictive monetary stance, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate cash flows, which in turn predicts negative S&P 500 20-day forward returns.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of triggered episodes, or the predicted negative returns are not statistically distinguishable from zero (p > 0.10).

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) of greater than 2% coincident with a drop in housing starts (HOUST) below 1.2 million units for two months signals weakening aggregate demand, which is expected to depress earnings and drive negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 YoY < -2% AND HOUST < 1200 for 2 months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the correlation between the trigger and negative returns is not significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained rise in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) above 6.5% for three consecutive months indicates labor market slack, which reduces corporate profit margins and consumer spending power, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are not significantly negative during triggered periods (p > 0.10), or the trigger fires but returns are positive more than 40% of the time.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly decline in the industrial production index (INDPRO) of more than 0.8% for two consecutive months signals contraction in manufacturing output, which is expected to precede negative earnings revisions and thus negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO monthly change < -0.8% for 2 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered months, or the predictive power vanishes (Rank IC < 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp one-month increase in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) of 0.75 percentage points or more, combined with a concurrent rise in CPI inflation (CPIAUCSL) above 4%, signals a surprise hawkish shift that raises short-term yields and equity risk premia, predicting negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS monthly change >= 0.75% AND CPIAUCSL > 400 (index scale) in the same month
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day returns are positive in more than 70% of triggered events, or the event does not produce statistically significant negative returns (p > 0.10).

mechanism_narrative: A monthly acceleration in nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) growth above 0.5% after three consecutive months of deceleration below 0.2% signals a re-acceleration in labor market momentum, which is expected to support earnings and drive positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS monthly change < 0.2% for 3 months, then > 0.5% in the next month
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are not significantly positive during triggered months (p > 0.10), or the event fails to predict returns in out-of-sample tests.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous monthly decline in both real personal consumption expenditures (GDPC1) and housing starts (HOUST) of more than 1% and 10%, respectively, indicates a broad-based collapse in demand, which is expected to produce negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days regardless of the monetary policy regime.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 monthly change < -1% AND HOUST monthly change < -10% in the same month
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered months, or the correlation is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A persistent monthly increase in the industrial production index (INDPRO) of at least 0.6% for four consecutive months signals a broad-based supply-side expansion, which is expected to boost corporate earnings and drive positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are not significantly positive during triggered periods (p > 0.10), or the event fails to predict returns in more than 50% of triggered quarters.
